prompt: An architect publishes a rule that all front-end code must use one state library, decided with the platform team alone. Within a quarter, four of five front-end teams have exceptions. Which antipattern, and what was the alternative?
hint: Lesson 17, the memo and its exceptions.

choices.text: The gatekeeper; review each team's code for the library
choices.why: Reviewing everyone's code is the gatekeeper itself, not a cure for a decision taken without the teams.

choices.text: The ivory tower; seek the affected teams' advice before deciding
choices.why: Right: the advice process, with the exceptions' reasons arriving before the rule instead of after.
The fault is in how the rule was made, not in the size of the design.

choices.text: The PowerPoint architect; draw the rule on a diagram
choices.why: A drawing of the rule would not have asked anybody anything.

prompt: A platform team builds a multi-cloud abstraction layer so that the company "could move off its cloud provider". No move is planned, and every service now pays a layer of indirection. Which antipattern is it?

choices.why: Somebody designed a great deal here, on purpose.
Right: building for a problem the company does not have, paid by every service.
Nothing says the teams were not asked; the problem is the size of the answer.
The layer was built and runs; it is not a drawing that the code fails to match.

prompt: A company has no architect. Each team picked its own way to authenticate service calls, and there are now four. A security review asks which one is the standard. What does lesson 17 say the alternative would have been?

choices.text: A central team that approves every service-to-service call
choices.why: That trades the absent architect for the gatekeeper.

choices.text: A complete security architecture written before any service is built
choices.why: Big design up front is the other extreme lesson 2 warned about.

choices.text: An owner for that cross-team decision, and a record of it
choices.why: Right: decision rights plus a decision record, just enough design for what crosses teams.

choices.text: Letting the four approaches compete until one wins on its own
choices.why: That is the accident continuing; nothing decides, so nothing wins.

prompt: Put the parts of the lesson's analysis of each antipattern in the order it uses them.
hint: Lesson 17: what you see, then why, then the bill, then the way out.

prompt: Lesson 17's one question for telling a drawing from a wish: can the person who drew this arrow point to the ___ where it lives?
Match each antipattern to the alternative lesson 17 gives for it.

pairs.right: draw what exists, dated, beside the code
run the decision through the advice process
automate the checkable rules and review only what crosses teams
design for the measured need and record what was not built
